Subject: Production token queueing + 500s on reserved pool

Ben —

We're seeing a sharp increase in 5xx errors and request queue times starting at ~07:20 PST. Our integration is on the reserved-plan pool (commit PLS-4821). Latency for customer-facing calls has jumped from ~120ms to 1.2s and we're getting intermittent 502/503 responses. This is happening during our morning batch traffic — it's impacting checkout flows.

We're in meetings with ops and finance; we need an ETA and whether Redwood will provide credits if SLA misses occur.

—Samir

Ben — quick triage notes (initial):

- Observed a ~3x spike in request arrival rate to PulseCommerce's tenant between 07:15–07:32 PST.
- Our telemetry shows that ~18% of those requests were routed to a fallback runpath (shared burst pool) due to a short-lived autoscaler race condition in the sharder — this increased effective concurrency on the shared pool and caused KV-cache thrashing.
- The reserved pool itself did not exhaust GPU memory, but headroom (concurrency slots) dropped below the canary threshold and we started returning 502s when the runtime failed fast on queuing.

Immediate remediation applied at 08:55 PST: disabled the autoscale handover for Pulse tenant and pinned routing back to their reserved nodes; raised per-tenant concurrency cap by 20% for a controlled window. Initial metrics after pinning show error rate dropping (see attached CSV).

Next steps (short):
1) Full host-level trace analysis (in progress) — ETA 3 hours.
2) Post-incident run to harden the autoscale state machine; will propose rollback-safe fix.
3) Real-time customer communication: recommend we offer an operational credit and a controlled retro rollout of the autoscaler fix.

I opened INF-2197 with the traces attached.

—Marcus
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

Samir —

First, thank you for the quick heads-up and for the request ids. Marcus's team has applied an immediate mitigation and we're actively running a trace analysis. We're coordinating internally on a remediation timeline and will share a concrete RCA and ETA by tomorrow EOD.

What we can confirm now:
- We routed some burst traffic to shared capacity due to an autoscaler race; that path had lower concurrency guarantees which explains the spikes in 502/503.
- We've pinned your tenant to reserved hosts and error rate is down compared to the peak.

Operational next steps we're proposing:
1) A temporary billing credit for the impacted window — I'll coordinate with finance.
2) A joint post-mortem next week (SLA/RCA + engineering runbook changes).
3) If helpful, a short-term manual increase in concurrency for your reserved pool while we harden the autoscaler.

Can you confirm a good time tomorrow (Tue) for a 30-minute sync? Also, any internal IDs you want referenced for procurement/finance (so we can route credits quickly)?

Thanks — Lauren
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
